prompt:
[quiet, tired] Ten p.m. The entrance is locked, the elevator is on night mode. Twelve floors and me.

Rounds. Stairs, floors, basement. Flashlight, keys, and nobody.

[quiet, uneasy] It smelled of wax by the server room. A warm strip of light ran out from under the door.

[quiet, tired] Locked. There was no server-room key on the ring.

Probably the emergency light. I went back up.

[quiet, warm] A cat by the dumpsters. Frank wrote about her for twenty years. I'll log her too.

[quiet, tired] Someone left the lights on on ten. I'll switch them off from the console.

[casual] Sure. Come on down.

[quiet, uneasy] I didn't ask what he could hear up there.

[quiet, tense] Static. Just in the corner, by the door. As if someone were standing there.

The elevator moved on its own. Nobody at the console. Must be a sensor.

[polite, curious] Thanks. Have you been here long?

[quiet, tired] Half past two. The logbook was still lying there, closed.

[quiet, tense] Another button had appeared on the console. Thirteen. A minute ago it wasn't there.

[whispering, terrified] Footsteps. Not on the cameras anymore. In the lobby.

The static took the shape of a face. It was looking straight into the lens.

[quiet, relieved] Yes. It's me.

[quiet, tired] I put the phone down without a word.

[friendly, old man] Security, it's Gus again. Got a kettle in that booth? Frank always left me one.

[calm, dreamy, a bit odd] Nah, I'll stay up here. It's quiet. You can hear real well up here…

[friendly, warm, old man] Ah, the new guy. Here, have an apple. From my garden.

[kind, reassuring, old man] Old building. You see all sorts of things. Just don't let it get to you.

[quiet, sad, old man] Thirty years. My wife worked here, on seven. Now I'm the one mopping.
[quiet, sweet, uncertain] Ethan?.. Is that you?
